settings.name_in_paper: Cost-aware pairwise pure exploration with fixed confidence (exponential family rewards)
unmapped: Each arm also has an unknown cost distribution with mean c_a >= 0 (possibly zero); costs are observed with rewards
Objective is the expected cumulative cost sum_a c_a E[N_a(tau)] subject to delta-correctness, not the sample complexity
Task is any pairwise exploration task (answer determined by a set of pairwise mean comparisons), e.g. BAI, ranking, top-m
Means assumed without ties (bandit model belongs to exactly one partition)
settings.definition_quote: a pure exploration task $(\calG, \varphi)$ can be defined through a partition ... A task $(\calG, \varphi)$ is a pairwise exploration task if for any $\calG_m \in \calG$, there exists a subset $\mathcal{I}_m$ ... the designed strategy should guarantee that the decision rule outputs the correct index $m$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ ... while minimizing the expected incurring cost $\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{c}, \boldsymbol{\mu};\tau)]=\sum_{a\in \calA} c_a \mathbb{E}[N_a(\tau)]$

settings.name_in_paper: Cost-aware pairwise pure exploration, Bernoulli bandits
unmapped: Arm-specific cost distributions with nonnegative means; objective is expected cumulative cost
Task is any pairwise exploration task
settings.definition_quote: Let $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ be a Bernoulli bandit model. ... using the stopping rule given in \Cref{for:stoppingrule} on Bernoulli bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Ranking identification in 3-armed 1-Gaussian bandits with cost vector equal to the gaps
unmapped: Task is identifying the full ranking of the arms
Cost of each arm equals its suboptimality gap, so cumulative cost is the regret incurred before stopping

settings.name_in_paper: Regret minimization via explore-then-commit (BAI with gaps as costs)
settings.definition_quote: with $\delta = 1/T$ and an explore-then-commit (ETC) scheme (i.e., keep pulling the identified arm after commitment), CAET achieves $R_{\bmu}(T)\leq \theta T^*(\boldsymbol{\Delta},\bmu)\log(T)$

algorithms.name: CAET with explore-then-commit (delta = 1/T, costs = estimated gaps)

symbols.T_star_c: cost-aware characteristic time T*(c,mu), with T*(c,mu)^{-1} = sup_{omega in Sigma_P} inf_{lambda in Alt(c,mu)} sum_{a in P_G(c,mu)} omega_a d(mu_a,lambda_a)/c_a

conditions: bandit model mu in S (belongs to exactly one partition)

source.label: the:lower-bound
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and give a pairwise exploration task $(\calG,\varphi)$. For any $\delta$-PAC strategy and any bandit model $\boldsymbol{\mu}\in S$, the following holds: $\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{c}, \boldsymbol{\mu};\tau_\delta)]\geq T^*(\boldsymbol{c},\boldsymbol{\mu})\kl(\delta,1-\delta)$

results.notes: Quantity is the expected cumulative cost sum_a c_a E[N_a(tau_delta)], recorded as 'other'. Paper also notes the consequences liminf E[f]/log(1/delta) >= T*(c,mu) and E[f] >= T*(c,mu) log(1/(2.4 delta)). With c=(1,...,1) it reduces to the Garivier-Kaufmann sample-complexity lower bound.

source.label: thm:inf-thre
source.quote: Let $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ be a Bernoulli bandit model. Let $\delta \in (0,1)$. For any sampling strategy, using the stopping rule given in \Cref{for:stoppingrule} on Bernoulli bandits with threshold $\beta(t,\delta)=\log(2tK(K-1)/\delta)$ ensures that for all $\boldsymbol{\mu} \in S$, $\Pb_{\bmu} (\tau_\delta < \infty, \varphi(\hat{\bmu}(\tau_\delta))\neq \varphi(\boldsymbol{\mu}))\leq \delta$.

results.notes: delta-correctness of the GLR stopping rule with any sampling rule; not tied to a specific algorithm, so algorithm left null.

tuning: threshold beta(t,delta) = log(C t^theta / delta) with a constant C = C(theta, K)

source.label: pro:Dev-Thre
source.quote: Let $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ be an exponential family of bandit models. Let $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $\theta >1$. There exists a constant $C=C(\theta, K)$ such that for any sampling strategy, using the stopping rule given in \Cref{for:stoppingrule} with threshold $\beta(t,\delta)=\log\left(Ct^\theta/\delta\right)$ ensures that for all $\bmu \in S$, $\Pb_{\bmu} (\tau_\delta < \infty$, $\varphi(\hat{\bmu}(\tau_\delta))\neq \varphi(\boldsymbol{\mu}))\leq \delta$.

results.notes: In the proof C is actually chosen as C_0 (e + log^{2K+1}(1/delta)), i.e. polylog in 1/delta, which is inconsistent with C = C(theta, K) in the statement.

symbols.T_star_c: cost-aware characteristic time T*(c,mu) from Theorem 1
symbols.theta: exponent of the threshold r(t)=O(t^theta), theta in [1, e/2]

conditions: mu in S (no ties among the compared arms)
tuning: truncation threshold gamma_0 log^{-r'}(1/delta) with 0 < r' < 1/8

source.label: thm:upperbound
source.quote: Let $\theta \in [1,e/2]$ and $r(t)=O(t^\theta)$. Using the stopping rule in \Cref{for:stoppingrule} with an exploration rate $\beta(t,\delta)=\log(r(t)/\delta)$ and the sampling rule in \Cref{for:sampling} with a sample distribution function $\boldsymbol{u}_\alpha$ under $\alpha=1-\log^{-r}(1/\delta)$, we have $\limsup\limits_{\delta \rightarrow 0}\dfrac{\mathbb{E}[f(\boldsymbol{c}, \boldsymbol{\mu};\tau_\delta)]}{\log(1/\delta)}\leq \theta T^*(\boldsymbol{c},\boldsymbol{\mu})$.

results.notes: Expected cumulative cost recorded as 'other'. Combined with Proposition 2, for exponential families CAET is delta-PAC with this guarantee for any theta>1. Specializations: positive-cost BAI recovers Kanarios et al. 2024; c=(1,...,1) recovers Garivier & Kaufmann sample complexity. Per-round optimization (computing omega*) is needed; paper notes computational cost.

source.label: thm:as-upper
source.quote: Let $\theta\in [1,e/2]$ and $r(t)=O(t^\theta)$. Using stopping rule given in \Cref{for:stoppingrule2} with $\beta(t,\delta)=\log(r(t)/\delta)$, the CAET algorithm ensures $\Pb_\mu\left(\limsup\limits_{\delta\rightarrow 0}\frac{f(\boldsymbol{c},\boldsymbol{\mu};\tau_\delta)}{\log(1/\delta)}\leq \theta T^*(\boldsymbol{c},\boldsymbol{\mu})\right)=1.$

results.notes: Almost-sure bound on the realized cumulative cost.

symbols.Delta_2: gap of the second-best arm mu_1 - mu_2
symbols.Delta_3: gap of the worst arm mu_1 - mu_3

conditions: K = 3, unit-variance Gaussian rewards, mu_1 > mu_2 > mu_3
cost vector equals the gap vector (0, Delta_2, Delta_3)

source.label: pro:three-arm
source.quote: Let $\delta\in (0,1)$. For any $\delta$-PAC algorithm under ranking identification with cost vector $\boldsymbol{\Delta}$. Any 3-armed 1-Gaussian bandits with reward expectations $\{\mu_1>\mu_2>\mu_3\}$ has: ... $T^*(\boldsymbol{\Delta},\boldsymbol{\mu})^{-1}=\frac{(\sqrt{\Delta_2}-\sqrt{\Delta_3})^2}{2}$ if $\Delta_3\leq [(3+\sqrt{5})/2]\Delta_2$ ... and $R(\tau_\delta)\geq T^*(\boldsymbol{\Delta},\boldsymbol{\mu})\kl(\delta,1-\delta)$.

results.notes: R(tau_delta) is the expected regret (gap-weighted pulls) before stopping, i.e. cumulative cost with costs = gaps; recorded as 'other'.

symbols.Delta_2: gap of the second-best arm mu_1 - mu_2
symbols.Delta_3: gap of the worst arm mu_1 - mu_3

conditions: K = 3, unit-variance Gaussian rewards, mu_1 > mu_2 > mu_3
cost vector equals the gap vector (0, Delta_2, Delta_3)

symbols.theta: threshold exponent, theta in [1, e/2] (theta > 1 for general exponential families)

tuning: commit to the identified arm after stopping

source.label: for:reg1
source.quote: with $\delta = 1/T$ and an explore-then-commit (ETC) scheme (i.e., keep pulling the identified arm after commitment), CAET achieves $R_{\bmu}(T)\leq \theta T^*(\boldsymbol{\Delta},\bmu)\log(T),\ T^*(\boldsymbol{\Delta},\bmu)=\sum\limits_{\Delta_a>0}\frac{\Delta_a}{\KL(\mu_a,\mu_1)}$

results.notes: Not a formal theorem; derived informally in the appendix from the asymptotic Theorem 2, dropping an additive constant term ('The last term can be bounded by a constant'). It is effectively an asymptotic (large T) bound, not an exact finite-T inequality. Costs are estimated gaps, which differs from the paper's main cost model.
